summary: Will you carry it: {the member} asks the player to put their own name on a bill and carry it in the room where it has to pass.
realLife: One life: Members who got bills signed into law pointed to partners across the aisle and in the other chamber: a nearly unanimous home-state group behind one court bill, a Senate committee chairman who carried a companion, a lead cosponsor of the other party. One said to start with the bipartisan bill and work with people. Another: A House member picked a Senate partner for her smart-cities bill because they shared the issue, constituents and a tech background, and because the home state was already a model. She said the choice depends on the topic and on who has shown interest. Another: When a bill's author leaves the legislature the bill stalls unless a current member or a committee is approved by the rules committee to take it over. Without that step the chamber may not act on it. Another: After two lawmakers resigned, their unfiled bill requests were claimed one by one by sitting members in both chambers, and a committee took one; several requests, including a large health idea, found no sponsor and were expected to die.
gates: The bill record shows a bill {the member} wrote that has no sponsor yet in the player's chamber, or a draft left by a member who has left the body.
The player holds a seat where the bill must be heard.
{the member} and the player are tied on the record by a shared committee, party, district interest or an old favor.
weights: How much the player's own seat and party help the bill get a hearing.
Whether the bill touches the player's district.
How many bills the player already carries.
Whether {the member} has carried one for the player.
Whether {chamber leader} would hold the bill against the one who carries it.
choices: agree and take it as your own
say you cannot carry it and name who could
say no and give the reason

branches.when: the player agrees to carry it
branches.then: The player's name goes on the bill record as its sponsor in the room, and the player now speaks for it in committee and on the floor.

branches.when: the player agrees on the condition of a change to the text
branches.then: The talk becomes a bargain over the bill's words; the change lands on the bill record and {the member} owes a favor.
The bill may find another sponsor or stall without one; the tie records who said no, and why.
The bill needs a member to take it over or it does not move at all; the one who takes it is written as its author.

branches.when: {chamber leader} signals the bill will be held
branches.then: The player learns that carrying it costs standing; the cost is read in the next committee assignment.
